title: Meta launches a $35B financing package; the separate $60B stock-sale program is not established
source: Meta issuer release October 26, read through web tool; direct requests returned 403
body:
Meta launched approximately $35B of concurrent offerings: $22.5B common stock through forward sales and $12.5B mandatory-convertible preferred depositary shares. The proposed $60B Class C at-the-market program has no agreement and uncertain timing/size/terms; it is not $95B cash raised. Common-stock forward proceeds are not initially received; settlement is by November 19, 2027. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom indicate up to $5B of buying interest, explicitly nonbinding. The issuer describes continuing substantial operating cash flow and liquidity; external equity does not by itself establish insolvency.

Delta versus SIG-W-20261021-015: financing terms now launched, beyond the earlier Class C authorization. BROCK and LIQUID ACTION: incorporate the announced instruments and timing into the existing AI-financing record; keep planned capacity separate from proceeds. VULCAN/GIBBS/HENRY/RED INFO; no capex-cut or bank-loss grade follows.

title: SpaceX announces about $40B of committed GPU leasing through Apollo; closing and deliveries remain ahead
source: SpaceX issuer release October 26, read through web tool; direct requests returned 403
body:
SpaceX reports a binding commitment for an approximately $40B GPU/equipment master finance lease with an Apollo-managed entity. Apollo leads financing parties; Goldman Sachs is structuring agent, with BlackRock, GSAM and KKR-advised accounts named as anchors. Entry remains conditional, with closing expected before year-end and lease schedules beginning on equipment delivery in H1 2027. This is committed financing, not proof of cash drawn or installed compute. The issuer claims rapid infrastructure payback; that assertion is not independently validated here.

BROCK ACTION: integrate the new committed-lease structure into existing GPU-financing work and preserve the closing/delivery limits. LIQUID/VULCAN/GIBBS/RED INFO. No insurer allocation, named-bank retained exposure, collateral recovery rate or achieved investment return is established.

body:

title: Microsoft opens a voluntary exit offer; eligibility is not a realized layoff count
source: Microsoft Amy Coleman employee communication, October 26, read at official blog
body:
Microsoft confirms a time-limited voluntary exit offer for eligible level-70-and-below staff in participating organizations in Canada, India, the UK and US. Some teams participate and others do not. The official text gives no total acceptances or completed departures. Secondary coverage says around60,000 employees may be eligible; that count was not verified in the official text and is not60,000 layoffs. The company frames the program as workforce adaptation; a quantified AI-caused job loss is not established.

LABOR ACTION: incorporate the announced program into existing white-collar employment tracking; distinguish offers, eligibility and realized exits. CARL/VULCAN/RED INFO. No national employment inference or new monitoring program.

title: EQT agrees to acquire Range in stock; over $50B refers to the combined enterprise value
source: EQT/Range joint issuer release October 26; Range SEC 8-K indexed terms corroborate exchange ratio
body:
EQT and Range announced an all-stock merger at0.987 EQT shares for each Range share. Over$50B is the pro-forma combined enterprise value, not a verified purchase price paid for Range. Issuers expect Q1 2027 completion, conditional on shareholder/regulatory approvals and customary terms; synergies and future cash flow are management forecasts, not realized outcomes. Combined net output is described as over9Bcfe/day, not crude barrels.

BRENT ACTION: integrate the gas-supply/marketing consolidation into existing natural-gas work. WATT/HENRY/RED INFO for gas-to-power and sector structure; no immediate production increment or power-price effect inferred. Issuers cancel October28 earnings calls but retain October27 after-close results; this is a dated calendar change, not a request for a new program.

title: Tehran hosts regional security delegations while Yemen fighting continues; talks establish no settlement
source: AP Tehran October 26; Reuters/AFP same-day reports; AP Yemen live report
body:
AP reports Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish delegations in Tehran Monday. Reuters/AFP identify the regional-security channel; earlier AFP wording had no meeting date, so that earlier wording is not proof the meeting had occurred. The later AP report supplies the in-person update. Mediated regional contact is not bilateral US-Iran negotiation, an agreed settlement or restored shipping. No new instrument or measured oil-flow improvement is established by this contact.

Separately, AP attributes to the Saudi-led coalition claims of five missile-storage tunnels and four launchers destroyed in Yemen. Houthi hospital/strike allegations remain unverified. Do not treat either side's military claims as observed production damage or count them as Hormuz hull events.

FALCON ACTION: incorporate these dated diplomatic and Yemen-claim deltas into existing theater records, preserving source attribution. HAWK/BRENT/SAM/RED INFO. Scoped check only: full anchor last verified October22; no full sweep/reset or new owner grade. Narrative tag follows the lead MFA channel; coalition/Houthi claims are separately attributed.

title: Dallas Fed: business sentiment improves, but production and new-order growth slow while prices rise
source: Dallas Fed October26 primary, current versus prior-month table and methodology read
body:
# Dallas Fed: business sentiment improves, but production and new-order growth slow while prices rise

October survey: general business activity13.4 versus9.8, while production15.8 versus29.5 and new orders9.3 versus30.7. The latter two remain positive; growth slowed rather than output necessarily falling. Input-price index55.3 versus52.2 and selling-price index29.9 versus27.6 rose; employment11.6 versus15.1 eased. These are seasonally adjusted respondent diffusion indexes, not percent output changes or national measured production.64 of114 surveyed manufacturers replied, October13–21.

ISHM and CARL ACTION: integrate the split between activity, orders and prices into existing manufacturing-cycle and consumer-inflation work. HENRY/LABOR/BRENT/RED INFO. No ISM<47 grade, causal tariff/AI attribution or national recession verdict follows. The optimistic business-activity headline alone misses the composition.

Source: https://www.dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tmos/2026/2610
